'''Agriworld-2079''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located on the spinward edge of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. Originally, it was the ancestral homeworld of a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Skrilling/Legends|primitive nomadic herders]]. The [[M'shinn]] from [[Genassa/Legends|Genassa]] later colonized the planet. The newcomers fenced in the nomadic herders, claimed their land, and left the peaceful aliens to figure out how to survive. Since that time, the original names of the inhabitants and their homeworld were lost to history, and the M'shinni imposed their own names instead. The planet became one of several vital M'shinni [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworlds]], producing a vast array of agricultural products that were shipped throughout the galaxy.

==Description==
===Planetology===
Agriworld-2079 was a terrestrial<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="CE">{{CSWECite|III|160|Skrilling}}</ref> located in the eponymous [[Agriworld-2079 system/Legends|star system]], a part of the [[M'shinni sector/Legends|M'shinni sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the spinward edge of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="UAA" /> The world's surface was largely flat, with [[Grass/Legends|grasslands]] inhabited by swift grazing animals. Its rich soils and consistent climate created a natural potential to produce a vast array of agricultural products.<ref name="GG12" />

===Inhabitants and society===
====Primordial species====
{{Main|Skrilling/Legends}}
[[File:Skrilling_UAA.jpg|thumb|left|180px|The native inhabitants of the planet were extremely low-tech people who filled the ecological niche of scavengers]]
The [[Skrilling/Legends|native species]] evolved on the flat [[Grass/Legends|grasslands]]. These were stocky [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with baggy, wrinkled gray skin and<ref name="GG12" /> [[Limb/Legends|hands]] with three stubby fingers.<ref name="NEGAS" /> They filled the niche of [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]], feeding on the carcasses of the swifter grazing [[Sentience/Legends|animals]]. Their metabolism was specifically tailored to digest spoiled and rotten [[Diet/Legends|meat]]<ref name="GG12" /> that would make other beings [[Death/Legends|deathly]] sick.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] were small and deeply set,<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="AA" /> resulting in poor eyesight; they instead relied upon a keen sense of smell to locate the decaying meat on which they fed.<ref name="GG12" /> They do not have a nostrils or [[Nose/Legends|nose]], instead breathing through a set of eight tubes that vertically line the fronts of their faces.<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="AA" /> The breather tubes had olfactory buds and several glands that secreted a mild [[Acid/Legends|acid]] to break down the rotten meat they preferred. These tubes could also be used as a defense mechanism, although the acid was a mild irritant and did not pose any true danger unless it made contact with one's eyes.<ref name="GG12" /> Their [[Mouth/Legends|mouths]] had multiple rows of needle-sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]]. Their bald heads featured a short [[Bone/Legends|bony]] crest that ran from their foreheads to the nape of the neck. This structure was used by infants to saw their way out of the [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] from which they were hatched.<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="AA" /><ref name="NEGAS" />

They had no technology of their own and thus usually relied on «secondhand» or rejected equipment. They carried only what they needed, making a living by collecting surplus or damaged technology, either repairing it to the best of their ability or gutting it for parts. The typical Skrilling had a smattering of repair skills – generally just enough to patch things back together temporarily.<ref name="GG12" />

====M'shinni colonies====
{{Main|M'shinn}}
[[File:Mshinni.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The M'shinn species from Genassa completely controlled the planet, without regard for its original inhabitants]]
When [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] from [[Genassa/Legends|Genassa]], the homeworld of<ref name="GG12" /> the aggressive agriculturalist<ref name="AA" /> species [[M'shinn]]i, arrived on the planet,<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="AA" /><ref name="UAA" /> they found that only a peaceful<ref name="AA" /> native species inhabited it. The natives lived an extremely low-tech existence as nomadic herders and possessed few manufactured goods. The M'shinni sought to realize the potential of the world's rich soils and rapidly divided the land into large agricultural plots, introducing intensive, high-tech [[Farm/Legends|farming]] that relied on extensive [[Droid/Legends|droid]] labor. The balance of the world was forever changed;<ref name="GG12" /> the vast herds were fenced in, their land was claimed, and the peaceful natives were forced to abandon their nomadic way of life.<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="UAA" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> The planet eventually came completely under M'shinni control. They designated it Agriworld-2079 and gave the original inhabitants the derogatory name «Skrilling» (meaning «Bone Picker»). Over time, even the natives themselves forgot what they had once called their own species and homeworld. Due to their natural ability to ingratiate themselves with others, the Skrillings soon integrated into the M'shinni colonies<ref name="GG12" /> on the world and became a permanent beggar class.<ref name="AA" />

Whenever a new world was [[Terraforming/Legends|terraformed]] or colonized by the M'shinni, the newly formed economic zones were divided among the [[Rootline]]s. This system formed the foundation of M'shinn politics and society, where each Rootline controlled a particular business and functioned almost like a family-owned corporation. On each world controlled by the M'shinni, these rules were monitored by the [[Council of the Wise]], composed of the eldest member of each Rootline on that planet. Agriworld-2079 was heavily mechanized, with few industrial areas consisting mainly of complexes that manufactured agricultural and harvesting droids as well as processed and packaged agricultural products. This industries that did exist were all owned by competing M'shinni Rootlines and were clustered around the [[Spaceport/Legends|starports]].<ref name="GG12" />

Due to their [[Symbiosis/Legends|symbiotic]] relationship with [[Plant/Legends|plants]], M'shinn technology had two main foci: [[Star/Legends|solar]] power and agriculture. The M'shinni combined the [[Scientist/Legends|sciences]] of engineering and botany in some unusual ways, producing solar collectors and power generators that were based on organic, cellular technologies. M'shinn technology could be found on numerous colony-world farms.<ref name="GG12" />

==History==
===Colonisation===
Long before the final years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="GG12" /> by around [[3966 BBY/Legends|3966 BBY]],<ref name="MshinniInterstellar">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'' establishes that the [[Skrilling/Legends|Skrillings]] first traveled off-world after the [[M'shinn]]i had [[Colonist/Legends|colonized]] their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] Agriworld-2079&mdash;which ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places in a [[Agriworld-2079 system/Legends|star system]] other than the [[Genassa system/Legends|Genassa system]]. The ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'' establishes that [[Jervo Thalien]]&mdash;whom [[Knights of the Old Republic 1|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 1]] depicts as a Skrilling&mdash;was [[Chairman/Legends|chairman]] of the off-world company [[Lhosan Industries]] by the time [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] became a member [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Since ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' dates the latter event to [[3966 BBY/Legends|3966 BBY]], the M'shinni must have therefore acquired interstellar travel ability at some point by that date.</ref> population pressures on the [[M'shinn]]i homeworld of [[Genassa/Legends|Genassa]] forced them to begin [[Colonist/Legends|colonizing]] space. With the discovery of the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], the M'shinni were able to expand in earnest; they «seeded» a number of nearby [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] with colonists and «harvested» their resources. Eventually, they controlled hundreds of worlds in what came to be known as the [[M'shinni sector/Legends|Mossonian sector]] (although its formal name was the M'shinni sector).<ref name="GG12" />

[[File:Genassa-EGTW.jpg|left|thumb|250px|The M'shinni space where Agriworld-2079 was located]]
At the time of expansion, the M'shinni discovered a [[Grass/Legends|grassland]] world with rich soils and a consistent climate that created natural potential for producing a vast array of agricultural products. On the planet, M'shinni [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] found only a peaceful native species of [[Skrilling/Legends|nomadic herders]] that was extremely primitive. Without regard for the original inhabitants, the M'shinni, who wanted to realize the world's natural potential, rapidly divided the land into large agricultural plots and introduced high-tech [[Farm/Legends|farming]].<ref name="GG12" /> The balance of the world was forever changed: the planet's vast herds were fenced in, and the natives were forced to give up their nomadic way of life.<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="UAA" /><ref name="NEGAS" /> The planet eventually came completely under M'shinni control. They designated it Agriworld-2079 and gave the original inhabitants the derogatory name «Skrilling». Over time, even the natives themselves forgot what they had once called their own species and homeworld.<ref name="GG12" /> Within a few generations,<ref name="AA" /><ref name="UAA" /> as a result of oppression,<ref name="NEGAS" /> the Skrillings integrated themselves into M'shinni colonies on the world as a permanent beggar class.<ref name="AA" />

The area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] that the M'shinni inhabited was first explored by the general [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] community between [[3000 BBY]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> and when the M'shinni first encountered the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], they quickly accepted the huge [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government and fully integrated themselves with the rest of galactic society.<ref name="GG12" /> From there, the Skrillings also expanded beyond their homeworld into modern, spacefaring [[Galactic community|society]].<ref name="GG12" /><ref name="UAA" />

The entire M’shinni sector remained part of the Galactic Republic until its final days. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], it was situated within the Republic's borders.<ref name="TEA" /> At that time, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ord Enisence/Legends|Ord Enisence]] hailed from the planet Agriworld-2079.<ref name="TCW Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Into a vital agriworld===
[[File:Skrilling_GG12.jpg|thumb|right|200px|During the Galactic Empire, a handful of Skrillings agitated for their freedom]]
With the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the outbreak of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the M'shinni sector was valued as an important source of food for nearby [[Sector/Legends|sectors]]. Agriworld-2079 became one of several vital M'shinni [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworlds]]. Its rich soils and consistent climate produced a vast array of [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]], [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]], and [[Grain/Legends|grains]], which were shipped throughout the galaxy. The planet was heavily mechanized but had few industrial areas. These complexes manufactured agricultural and harvesting droids and processed and packaged agricultural products.<ref name="GG12" />

While many of the Skrillings spread out into the galaxy, a number still lived on the planet. Most were servants and low-level employees of the M'shinni Rootlines that ran the planet, but in recent [[Standard year/Legends|years]] a handful began to agitate for their freedom. Given the Skrillings' tendency to avoid open conflict, it was unlikely that this would evolve into an armed rebellion, although there was always a chance that the Skrillings would wheedle outside forces into acting on their behalf.<ref name="GG12" />

==Behind the scenes==
Agriworld-2079 was first mentioned in the [[1995]] [[West End Games]] sourcebook for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', ''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'', in an entry authored by [[Lisa Smedman]].<ref name="GG12" /> The [[2003]] supplement to the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' published by [[Wizards of the Coast]], ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', placed Agriworld-2079 in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="UAA" /> The [[2006]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', published by [[Del Rey]], was the first to provide an image of many alien homeworlds, including the Skrillings' planet.<ref name="NEGAS" /> In [[2009]], the [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|online appendix]] to the reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] placed the Agriworld-2079 system, and therefore the planet itself, in grid square L-7.<ref name="EAOC" /> However, the [[2010]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Official Episode Guide Series 1 & 2|reference book]] for the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first]] and [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second]] seasons of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] television series incorrectly placed Agriworld-2079 in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="CWEG">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Official Episode Guide Series 1 & 2]]''</ref>

The ''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]'' sourcebook, in its entry on Skrillings, suggested a plot hook in which the gamemaster might introduce the characters to Skrillings who were trying to regain control of their homeworld. These Skrillings were looking for muscle to back up their demands for sovereignty or needed assistants for a hit-and-run raid on one of the M'shinni Rootlines that had taken over their planet.<ref name="GG12" />
